verdict.line: You lose extended trades and solo kills before level 6 if you let Granite Shield reset between pokes, but the 53% head-to-head over 3186 games says you win the game once Siphoning Strike stacks and Trinity Force come online.

brief.thesis: Malphite's passive Granite Shield absorbs the chip damage from your short-range Siphoning Strike, so early poke and all-in trades favor him even though the overall matchup win rate (53%, 3186 games) favors you. The lane flips once you've stacked enough Q kills and completed your core items, because nothing in his kit scales to punish a six-item Nasus the way it punishes a level-4 one.

theirWindow.when: when his Granite Shield is up
theirWindow.what: He trades for free here — Seismic Shard (Q, 625 range) slows you into stick range and Brutal Strikes (W) buffs his AD, so back off and farm instead of contesting.

yourWindow.when: right after you land a hit on him
yourWindow.what: Granite Shield only recharges if he hasn't been hit recently, so the auto or Q that breaks it opens a clean window to follow with Wither (W) and a full trade.

start.why: Flat damage reduction on the first attack from a champion each 5s directly answers Seismic Shard pokes and Ground Slam chip, and it's the dominant start here at 52.6% over 2980 games.

boots.why: The ability haste shortens Wither and Spirit Fire cooldowns, letting you reset the armor-shred zone and the slow more often in extended trades; 53.1% over 2135 games.

core.why: This is the single biggest power spike in the whole matchup — it's what turns a losing lane into the 59.1% win rate seen in the top build path.
Armor and attack speed slow blunts Malphite's Brutal Strikes-buffed autos and softens Ground Slam's armor-scaled magic damage.
Stacks with Soul Eater lifesteal to turn Siphoning Strike farming into real sustain against his poke; completes the 59.1%-over-469-games path.

the game runs long and you need more omnivamp and raw tank stats

runes.keystoneWhy: The on-move healing offsets Seismic Shard chip damage better than anything else listed, since Malphite's entire early plan is poking you down with a ranged slow you can't itemize against directly.

summoners.why: Flash+Ghost has the highest measured win rate in this matchup (55.2%) and directly answers Unstoppable Force — Flash dodges the knockup, Ghost closes distance to punish him once his shield is down. Ghost+Teleport (50.4% pick, 51.5% win rate) is the safer alternative if you want to prioritize split-pushing once Trinity Force comes online.

playing.title: Farm stacks outside Q range
playing.detail: Don't stand in Seismic Shard's 625 range to last-hit if you don't have to — every free poke he lands resets Granite Shield and denies you a trade.

playing.title: Trade only after you've hit him
playing.detail: Granite Shield only recharges when he hasn't taken damage recently, so land a Q or auto first, then commit Wither and the rest of your combo.

playing.title: Drop Spirit Fire under his all-in
playing.detail: When he commits Brutal Strikes and Ground Slam, place Spirit Fire (E, 12s cooldown) on the fight — the armor reduction plus the flat damage swings close trades your way.

playing.title: Respect Unstoppable Force at level 6
playing.detail: His R is a 1000-range dash with a knockup on a 130s cooldown at rank 1 — don't overextend past mid-lane alone once he's six, since one landed R can snowball into a kill.

playing.title: Wither any extended chase
playing.detail: Wither (W, 700 range) decelerates both his move and attack speed over time, which directly neutralizes a Brutal Strikes-buffed Malphite trying to stick to you or run.

playing.title: Prioritize Trinity Force completion
playing.detail: The matchup measurably flips once Trinity Force is finished — this is the item that turns your stacked Q damage and sustain into actual lane dominance.

playing.title: Split push once ahead on items
playing.detail: A scaled Nasus with Fury of the Sands threatens towers far better than Malphite's frontline engage can defend them — use Teleport or Ghost to capitalize on side lanes.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/sample-size figures above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG — only the tactical reasoning (why each pick matters, when to trade, how the cooldowns interact) is my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Try not to get hit by Malphite’s (Q) too often. Heal back up with [Q] and control lane to focus on gaining more [Q] stacks.
